required_fixes: Frozen validity threshold null_std>0.01 is structurally incompatible with trajectory-grouped permutation variance at N=1999 / 24 strata. K=12->K=24 moved std only 0.00941->0.00967 (+0.00026), still below 0.01 by 0.00033. Independent replication with doubled variants 3->6 moved std 0.0046->0.00649 still below 0.01. Permutation std scales DOWN with N per stratum, so larger N will worsen, not fix, degeneracy. A new preregistration must either lower or replace the absolute 0.01 std floor with a distribution-aware degeneracy check or analytic Dirichlet-Multinomial bias model before claiming SURVIVES/FALSIFIED on this FSM class.

Positive control expectation that K=24 at N=1999 would achieve |null_mean|<0.1 and null_std>0.01 was half-correct: mean 0.1297->0.0748 now passes, but std 0.0104 prediction failed (observed 0.00967). The prereg sensitivity calculation conflated prior smoothing bias (K-dependent) with permutation variance (N/strata-dependent). Fix requires separating bias floor calibration (K/alpha) from null variance calibration (permutation design, strata coarseness, trajectory count).

Independent-noise control remains degenerate (null_std 0.00649<0.01) despite RECALIBRATED 6 variants per state (36 unique hashes identical cardinality to correlated). If independent is to serve as valid discrimination control per G2, design must raise within-stratum DOM diversity (fewer trajectories with longer lengths, coarser C, or more variants) or relax std threshold for low-diversity nulls without weakening confound detection.

No new Gate0 production SPA data is required for this calibration fix, but claim ceiling remains bounded to locally-hosted 6-state SHA256 hash truncation. Any future SURVIVES must be accompanied by transfer test to non-hash, visual/computed-style DOM or production session-correlated SPA before physics mechanism can inform product regime detectors.
